text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HAARETZ
- Foreign Minister Levy once again considering resigning. "I do not trust Netanyahu".
- Senior Bank of Israel official: Our policy is to let the forces of the market determine the exchange rate.
- Printing press worker suspected of stealing matriculation Bible exam.
JERUSALEM POST
- Labour legislator Sneh: Arafat ordered enhanced security cooperation.
- Levy, prime minster row delays reshuffle.
- Netanyahu condemns anti-Islam leaflets. Islamic movement protests Hebron flyers.
- Phone competition hits last-minute trouble.
- Central bank: 1997 budget deficit higher than government's target.
- Israel will ask United States to expand free trade pact into Jordan.
MAARIV
- Defence Minister Mordechai proposes that French troops replace Israeli soldiers in south Lebanon.
- Foreign Minister Levy considering resigning.
- Police say hundreds of high-school students bought Bible matriculation exam.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Cabinet minister Sharon: If I'm not appointed to the inner cabinet, I will refuse to serve as finance minister.
- Arafat: Sharon has not called me a "war criminal" recently.
GLOBES
- Bank of Israel: We will intervene in foreign currency trading as necessary.
- The anti-monopoly authority raided Bezeq offices; managers will be questioned over rate cuts.
- Supersol in negotiations over sale of chain in Hungary; deal estimated at 20 to 25 million dollars.
